messages:
Elena (partnerships): Heads-up — thinking about introducing a 'usage accelerator' clause for marketplace private offers when we co-sell with SIs/hardware partners. Credits vest on two milestones: SI onboarding + usage thresholds. Need legal, marketplace, and ops alignment before pitching partners.

Sam (revenue_ops): Love the idea. Need to model unit economics — what's the assumed ramp (90d/180d)? Also, credits vs permanent discount: which preserves margin better? :thinking_face:

Jen (marketplace_ops): FYI marketplace constraints: AWS and GCP marketplace often don't accept conditional credits in the contract body. Usually we map to either a line-item discount, promotional coupon, or post-bill rebate depending on marketplace. We'll need per-cloud mapping.

Priya (sales_ops): On billing: we can create SKU `MKT-ACCEL-CREDIT` and attach expiry metadata. Implementation: credits consume against invoices until expiry. NOTE: renewals are messy — credits applied pre-renewal typically don't carry unless we explicitly allow carryover.

Mike (legal): High-level legal asks: exact milestone definitions, clawback mechanism if partner fails to onboard or account churns, and a hard expiry. Avoid vague terms like 'onboarding completed' — define deliverables. Draft clause below (first pass):

```
Accelerator Credit Clause (sample):
1) Onboarding Credit: On Partner's delivery of SI onboarding defined as (a) SI deployment into production, (b) customer acceptance test signed, and (c) activation in our telemetry, Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to X USD to Customer's account.
2) Usage Credits: Monthly credits will be released if Customer's billable usage in the preceding 30 days exceeds the stated threshold (Y tokens). Credits expire 12 months from issuance.
3) Clawback: If Customer reduces committed spend by >50% within 6 months after credit issuance, Redwood reserves the right to offset future credits and invoice the unamortized portion of the onboarding credit.
4) Marketplace Mapping: For offers transacted via Cloud Marketplaces, credits will be reflected as one of the marketplace's supported primitives (coupon, post-sale rebate, or line-item discount).
```

Sam (revenue_ops): If we do credits instead of discounts, partner reporting changes — credits look like promotional spend vs margin lowering. Also HW co-invest question: can a hardware partner subsidize onboarding credit? Need clarity on accounting treatment.

Elena (partnerships): Proposal: split accelerator into two buckets so it's easier operationally and legally — (1) Onboarding credits (one-time, co-funded if HW partner agrees) and (2) Usage credits (recurring monthly tranche released when usage thresholds hit). Onboarding = coupon/promo, Usage = recurring discount or post-bill rebate depending on marketplace.

Jen (marketplace_ops): That split is good. Practical: onboarding credit -> coupon/promo SKU; usage credit -> recurring discount line. I'll confirm exact primitives per AWS/GCP/Azure tomorrow.

Priya (sales_ops): Operational rules we should lock down now: auto-expire credits at 12 months; set ledger tag `accelerator_v1`; disallow carryover unless renewal meets trigger. Suggested renewal trigger: if renewal booking >= 80% of prior committed spend, release final tranche.

Sam (revenue_ops): I'll run three econ sims (fast ramp 90d, medium 180d, slow 365d) to show P&L impact and net CAC reduction with co-funding. Will post numbers by EOD. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Elena (partnerships): Action items: Mike -> push clause + clawback wording by EOD; Jen -> confirm marketplace primitive mapping per cloud by tomorrow; Priya -> confirm SKU/tag expiry mechanics and billing flow; Sam -> post econ sims. CC @deploy-bot please scaffold a template doc for partner offers. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Created placeholder doc at /templates/marketplace-accelerator-v1.md (edit & attach partner-facing language).

Elena (partnerships): Thanks all — if nothing else, please drop any 'deal-breaker' constraints here. If none, we'll aim to prototype this on one pilot partner next quarter. :rocket:
